label: PF Backlog 612
title: CI strategy: fast targeted per-change gate + scheduled full sweep (stop running full precheck on every change)
body:
Problem: every PR/merge currently runs precheck --full (58 gates, ~6-20 min), so any single fix pays the full suite cost and unrelated pre-existing red (e.g. committed learnings pollution, BI-PF-1332) blocks ALL merges. Observed: PR #93 (docs-only ADR) blocked by an unrelated pipeline test fail.

Proposal (industry shift-left model):
1. PR/change gate = targeted checks only: compile + lint/static + code review + the tests that cover the changed area (runtime-selected) + API/governance contract tests for touched routes.
2. A SEPARATE scheduled system runs the FULL suite/gates on develop every 30-60 min (10-20 min), surfacing cross-cutting regressions on the integration branch, not on every PR.
3. Merge-time still re-validates: conflicts/regressions are caught at merge or by the scheduled full run and fixed forward.

PF already has tiers (precheck fast vs --full) + core/validation_engine profiles (FEATURE_PR/INTEGRATION/DOGFOOD/RELEASE). Implement by: making the PR CI job run the fast/FEATURE_PR profile; adding a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (cron) running precheck --full on develop; keeping the release/merge profile as a deliberate, heavier gate. Preserve fail-closed for genuine new issues (baseline-aware gates so legacy debt does not block).

brief.problem: precheck --full on every PR is costly and lets unrelated red block all merges.
brief.what_adds: Fast targeted per-PR gate + scheduled full sweep on develop.
brief.why: Reduce change cost and unblock independent work without losing coverage.

objective: Cut per-change CI cost: fast targeted gate per PR + a scheduled full sweep on develop, without losing regression safety.
acceptance_criteria: PR CI runs a fast/targeted profile (changed-area tests + lint + contract) instead of precheck --full.
A scheduled workflow runs precheck --full on develop periodically and reports; failures are actionable.
Genuine new breakages are still fail-closed (baseline-aware); legacy/pre-existing red does not block unrelated PRs.
Measured: median PR gate time drops materially; scheduled full run remains green-or-reported.
